summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was readmitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting after a recent relapse in alcohol use. He presented unable to tolerate oral intake, with elevated liver enzymes and an anion gap metabolic acidosis that improved with IV fluids. Imaging confirmed fatty liver, splenomegaly, and portal flow reversal consistent with cirrhosis and portal hypertension, but no acute cholecystitis. His pain was managed with IV then oral hydromorphone, and his diet was advanced as symptoms improved. Liver function tests trended toward improvement by discharge, and he remained asymptomatic for alcohol withdrawal. He was discharged home on his baseline medications, including nadolol, spironolactone, lactulose, and omeprazole, with 30 tablets of oral hydromorphone for short-term pain control, and follow-up arranged with primary care and liver clinic. Social work assisted with addiction support planning.
